title: Flow-control and keyed retry contracts for global failover
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Different services and language SDKs have diverging retry/timeout/backoff behavior. This manifests as cascading latencies during partial regional outages, inconsistent idempotency usage (leading to duplicated side-effects), and unpredictable failover behavior when circuit-breakers open and load-shedding triggers. Goal: Define a single developer-facing contract and runtime behavior for retries, timeouts, backoff, idempotency keys, and hedged requests that is region-aware and aligns with SLO-driven load shedding and circuit-breaker policies. The contract must be implementable in the core runtime, the HTTP/gRPC gateway, and client SDKs (Node, Python, Go).
acceptance_criteria: A1: SDKs (Node/Python/Go) expose a single RetryPolicy interface with fields: max_attempts, base_backoff_ms, max_backoff_ms, jitter_strategy, hedged_request_window_ms, and idempotency_key_hint
A2: Runtime will apply region-aware backoff multipliers when a downstream region is degraded; multiplier derived from region health API and SLO tier mapping
A3: Hedged requests supported end-to-end: client can opt-in to hedging per call; runtime enforces single-response semantics and ensures KV-cache coherence for model stateful calls
A4: Circuit-breaker state is propagated to clients via standard headers; clients must stop retries when service-level circuit indicates Quarantine state
A5: Load-shedding decisions (reject vs degrade) are tied to SLO-slack metrics and are observable in the Console; dashboards and alerts created
A6: All changes covered by automated integration tests and e2e canary demonstrating graceful failover across regions with preserved idempotency semantics
decision_log: 2026-03-10: Chose single SDK RetryPolicy abstraction rather than language-specific heuristics to reduce developer errors
2026-03-11: Use 'keyed idempotency' convention: clients provide idempotency-key header; runtime also accepts auto-generated idempotency keys for safe read-only paths
2026-03-12: Hedged requests default: off. Allow opt-in with explicit hedged_request_window_ms. Hedging limited to idempotent or read-only operations until further review
2026-03-13: Circuit-breaker header format agreed: X-Runtime-CB-State: Open|HalfOpen|Closed and X-Runtime-CB-Reason
2026-03-13: Backoff multipliers per region to be read from /runtime/region-health with exponential ramp capped by max_backoff_ms
implementation_notes: SDK: implement RetryPolicy class with serialization to headers so gateways/runtime can reconstruct client intent
Gateway: honor client-specified hedged_request_window_ms but cap to 200ms for public tenants; dedicated tenants configurable
Runtime: map idempotency-key to request deduplication bucket; store minimal metadata (hash, TTL, response-pointer) with strict size cap
KV-cache: when hedged requests are used, ensure single writer semantics by routing all cache-populating attempts through a leader token per key
Circuit-breaker: runtime exposes CB state via response headers and a /metrics endpoint; clients must short-circuit retries when CB state is Open
Load-shedding: implement token-bucket per-tenant fallback that can return 429 with Retry-After when SLO slack exhausted
Telemetry: emit attempt_number, hedged=true/false, idempotency_key_present, region_origin, circuit_state fields for each request
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag SDK exposure behind 'global_retry_contract' flag; default off in GA
2) Deploy gateway header passthrough in staging; enable runtime mapping and dedupe in internal canary cluster
3) Run synthetic canary where 10% of traffic uses new headers and validate no duplication for idempotent endpoints
4) Gradually widen client SDK opt-ins: first internal services, then public SDKs via minor release notes
5) Monitor for increased 5xx/4xx and dedupe hit/miss ratios for 48 hours before full rollout
6) Announce deprecation plan for older per-service retry heuristics with 6-week window
test_plan: Integration: Simulate region latency spike and assert runtime uses region multiplier and backs off calls per policy
E2E Canary: Create an API that performs an idempotent write; assert exactly-once semantics under simultaneous hedged attempts
Chaos: Introduce circuit-breaker open state in region A and assert clients stop retries and fallback to region B when configured
Performance: Measure 95th/99th latency delta with hedged enabled vs disabled; ensure hedging does not regress P99 beyond SLO threshold
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: Retry attempts by service, idempotency dedupe rate, hedged request ratio, circuit-breaker transitions per region
Alerts: dedupe_miss_rate > 1% for 5m, hedged_success_without_duplication < 99% for 10m, circuit_open_rate spike correlating with increased retries
SLO: Error budget burn-rate integration: when burn-rate > 2x, load-shedding threshold should move from degrade->reject
Logs/Tracing: Include hedged_parent_id and idempotency_key in traces for distributed investigation
